title: Algorithmic randomness in harmonic analysis
summary: Within the last fifteen years, a program of establishing relationships between algorithmic randomness and almost-everywhere theorems in analysis and ergodic theory has developed. In harmonic analysis, Franklin, McNicholl, and Rute characterized Schnorr randomness using an effective version of Carleson's Theorem. We show here that, for computable $1<p<\infty$, the reals at which the Fourier series of a weakly computable vector in $L^p[-π,π]$ converges are precisely the Martin-Löf random reals.
